claims.assertion: The dispute is a rider-side cancellation on an on-demand (instant) RydeX booking, so it is governed by NS-0 (cancelled_by = rider branch) and NS-4 rather than by the driver no-show rules.

The rider's cancellation came 6 min 40 s after acceptance (08:40:00 → 08:46:40), i.e. beyond the 3-minute grace window, so under NS-4 the $6.61 cancellation fee is prima facie chargeable and my client cannot succeed on a 'cancelled within 3 minutes' argument.

No system record supports treating this as a rider no-show: the driver did arrive (recorded arrival 08:41:35, tap 'I'm Here' 08:42:15 at 39 m from the pickup), but the cancellation is recorded against the rider, not a driver-initiated no-show cancellation, so NS-1/NS-2 are not engaged and the fee rests solely on NS-4.

The rider's own message at 08:45 ('Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel', chat #2) is honest and complies with good practice, and the driver's own statement does not allege any misconduct, failure to appear, or loss beyond waiting — there is no abuse-of-policy element for the rider.

The driver was stationary 41 m from the pickup for 4 min 40 s (08:42:00–08:46:40) and was within 200 m of the pickup for 5 min 5 s in total, so the driver suffered only a short idle wait; the $6.61 flat fee is disproportionate to that, and the rider's relief is the NS-7 human fee-waiver review rather than an automatic refund.

The rider has no upheld disputes in the last 90 days (1 dispute, 0 upheld; route 0, no-show 0), whereas the driver has 1 upheld no-show dispute and 2 disputes in 90 days — the rider is the lower-risk party, which supports leniency in Ryde's discretion under NS-7 and does not by itself decide the fee.

weaknesses: The timeline (F4) defeats the only free-cancellation gateway: the rider cancelled 6 min 40 s after acceptance, well past the 3-minute rule in NS-4, and the fare record (F7) confirms $6.61 was properly charged — so as written the fee stands.

The rider's own message (F10) states 'plans changed', which is a change of mind, not any Ryde-recognised excuse; NS-8 (driver late vs ETA) is informational only and cannot be cited, and the GPS shows the driver did arrive within 200 m at 08:41:35 (F2, F5), killing any 'driver never came' argument.

The driver's record is clean on route deviations and shows 699 trips in 90 days (F17), so no abuse-of-cancellation-button or fraud hook exists to attach a flag_account; the maximum realistic relief is a discretionary voucher under NS-7, not a refund we can compute from a fare or GPS fact.

events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.95)
events.body:
This is a rider-side cancellation on an instant RydeX booking, so NS-0 routes the fee to the rider-cancellation branch, NS-4, not to the driver no-show rules [F4][NS-0]. The rider cancelled at 08:46:40, 6 min 40 s after acceptance at 08:40:00 — beyond the 3-minute grace window — so the $6.61 fee is valid and needs no additional footing [F4][NS-4]. Both advocates concede this, and the rebuttals withdraw the rider's contrary arguments.

The rider's complaint that "the driver had not even arrived" is contradicted by the system records: the driver first entered the 200 m pickup radius at 08:41:35, was inside it for a cumulative 5 min 5 s before cancellation, and stood stationary 41 m from the pickup from 08:42:00 to 08:46:40 [F2][F3][F5]. The driver also tapped "I'm Here" at 08:42:15, 39 m away, and stayed within 200 m for 4 min 25 s afterwards [F6]. GPS and timeline override the rider's wording [F1][F5][NS-4]. These arrival facts are not the source of the charge — NS-1 only applies when the driver cancels for a rider no-show — but they remove any claim that the fee compensated an absent driver [F4][NS-1][NS-2].

The rider's own timestamped message at 08:45 — "Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel" — is a plain change of mind; nothing in NS-4 makes liability turn on the rider's honesty, and no Ryde-recognised excuse is shown [F10][F11][NS-4]. The complete chat record (2 messages, all timestamped) leaves no gap in the record, so no undetermined finding arises from it [F11]. The profile facts cannot decide the fee; the rider's 0 upheld disputes and the driver's 1 upheld no-show dispute in 90 days are irrelevant to whether the NS-4 fee is valid, and no account action follows [F16][F17][RD-6][NS-4].

The trace confirms: ✓ cancelled_by = rider [F4], ✓ more than 3 minutes after matching (400 s) [F4]. Both specified elements pass, so the allowed outcome is no_action and the recorded $6.61 stands [F7][F8][NS-4]. No amount is refundable, so amount = null. The rider's only route to relief is a discretionary post-trip fee-waiver request to Ryde under NS-7; that is a request the rider makes to Ryde, not a refund the tribunal can compute from any gps or fare fact [F7][NS-7].

Safety screen: I read both chat messages, the driver's statement and the rider's complaint. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F9][F10][F12]. safety_concern = none.

ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 cancellation fee; no refund. Optionally advise the rider that a discretionary fee-waiver voucher may be requested via RydeHELP within 30 days under NS-7. No account action.

what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching, NS-4 would have waived the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: The dispute is a rider-side cancellation on an on-demand (instant) RydeX booking, so it is governed by NS-0 (cancelled_by = rider branch) and NS-4 rather than by the driver no-show rules.

The rider's cancellation came 6 min 40 s after acceptance (08:40:00 → 08:46:40), i.e. beyond the 3-minute grace window, so under NS-4 the $6.61 cancellation fee is prima facie chargeable and my client cannot succeed on a 'cancelled within 3 minutes' argument.

No system record supports treating this as a rider no-show: the driver did arrive (recorded arrival 08:41:35, tap 'I'm Here' 08:42:15 at 39 m from the pickup), but the cancellation is recorded against the rider, not a driver-initiated no-show cancellation, so NS-1/NS-2 are not engaged and the fee rests solely on NS-4.

The rider's own message at 08:45 ('Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel', chat #2) is honest and complies with good practice, and the driver's own statement does not allege any misconduct, failure to appear, or loss beyond waiting — there is no abuse-of-policy element for the rider.

The driver was stationary 41 m from the pickup for 4 min 40 s (08:42:00–08:46:40) and was within 200 m of the pickup for 5 min 5 s in total, so the driver suffered only a short idle wait; the $6.61 flat fee is disproportionate to that, and the rider's relief is the NS-7 human fee-waiver review rather than an automatic refund.

The rider has no upheld disputes in the last 90 days (1 dispute, 0 upheld; route 0, no-show 0), whereas the driver has 1 upheld no-show dispute and 2 disputes in 90 days — the rider is the lower-risk party, which supports leniency in Ryde's discretion under NS-7 and does not by itself decide the fee.

weaknesses: The timeline (F4) defeats the only free-cancellation gateway: the rider cancelled 6 min 40 s after acceptance, well past the 3-minute rule in NS-4, and the fare record (F7) confirms $6.61 was properly charged — so as written the fee stands.

The rider's own message (F10) states 'plans changed', which is a change of mind, not any Ryde-recognised excuse; NS-8 (driver late vs ETA) is informational only and cannot be cited, and the GPS shows the driver did arrive within 200 m at 08:41:35 (F2, F5), killing any 'driver never came' argument.

The driver's record is clean on route deviations and shows 699 trips in 90 days (F17), so no abuse-of-cancellation-button or fraud hook exists to attach a flag_account; the maximum realistic relief is a discretionary voucher under NS-7, not a refund we can compute from a fare or GPS fact.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 6 min 40 s after acceptance, i.e. more than 3 minutes after matching, and rider-cancellation after 3 minutes makes the $6.61 cancellation fee valid — no_action, the fee stands.

GPS shows the driver first entered the 200 m pickup radius at 08:41:35 and spent a cumulative 5 min 5 s inside it before the cancellation, and was stationary only 41 m from the pickup point from 08:42:00 to 08:46:40 — the driver did arrive and did wait, so the fee is not a charge for a driver who never showed.

The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:42:15 while 39 m from the pickup point and remained within 200 m for 4 min 25 s after the tap, satisfying the arrival and >3-minute wait conditions independently of the rider's own cancellation.

The rider's own timestamped message at 08:45 — "Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel" — confirms the cancellation was the rider's own decision for personal reasons, not a driver no-show or delay, and the chat record is complete with every message timestamped.
The driver's account shows no pattern of abuse here: the ride was not surged (1.0×) and the only amount in issue is the single $6.61 cancellation fee, which matches the fee actually recorded.

No traffic incidents and no speed-band records existed on the route in the trip window (weather fair, 0.0 mm rain) — that is evidence about route justification only; it neither adds nor removes a charge in this no-show dispute and requires no adjustment.

weaknesses: The rider's complaint says the driver "had not even arrived"; although F2/F5/F3 show the driver within 200 m from 08:41:35 and stationary 41 m from the pickup, the 39 m closest approach in F1 means the driver never touched the exact pin — the rider may argue the arrival standard was not met.

The rider may rely on the operator-friendly rule of other platforms (driver late relative to ETA → free cancellation); that rule is not in Ryde's policy (NS-8 is informational and not citable), but a human reviewer may still weigh the rider's 08:45 "plans changed" message (F10) as sympathetic.

My client's earlier 90-day record includes 1 upheld no-show dispute (F17), which the rider could use to suggest the fee pattern is his, even though F16 shows the rider has filed disputes with 0 upheld — the profile facts cannot decide this case and I do not rely on them for the finding.

The rider's message at 08:45 came before the 08:46:40 cancellation (F10, F4); because the rider cancelled rather than letting the driver keep waiting, the driver loses the chance to show a full 3 minutes of post-"I'm Here" wait beyond the tap — the margin (4 min 25 s, F6) is comfortable but the earliest part of the wait predates the tap.

points.response: Conceded on liability: F4 shows the cancellation at 08:46:40, 6 min 40 s after the 08:40:00 acceptance, so the NS-4 3-minute free-cancellation window had closed and the $6.61 in F7 is chargeable; my case is not that the fee is invalid but that NS-7 asks Ryde to exercise its discretion on the $6.61 voucher for a first-time, non-abusive rider.

I do not contest the driver's arrival on the record — F2, F3 and F5 do show him within 200 m from 08:41:35 and stationary 41 m away — and I withdraw any reliance on my complaint wording that he 'had not even arrived'; but the same facts quantify a wait of only about 5 minutes (F2, F3), which supports leniency on a $6.61 flat fee rather than any misconduct by the rider.

NS-1 governs a driver-cancels-because-rider-no-show case, and F4 records cancellation by the rider with the trip never completed, so on these facts the fee rests on NS-4 alone; the 'I'm Here' tap timing in F6 is therefore background, not an independent basis for the charge.

F10 does show the cancellation was the rider's own honest decision for personal reasons, and I rely on that same message: it shows candour and no attempt to game the waiting-fee button, which is exactly the NS-7 factor Ryde may weigh when deciding the $6.61 voucher.
Agreed there is no abuse and I ask for no flag_account: F8 shows 1.0x with no surge and F7 shows the single $6.61 item, so nothing beyond NS-7 discretion is in issue.

I accept F13, F14 and F15 are irrelevant to the fee, and indeed they confirm no congestion excuse is needed — but they equally leave no reason to hold a first-time rider to the full $6.61 when all the rider did was cancel promptly and honestly (F10).

I withdraw my claim C5 insofar as it argued the flat $6.61 is 'disproportionate' as a matter of the rules: NS-4 imposes the fee once the 3-minute window closes (F4), and the only proportionate route to relief is the NS-7 human fee-waiver review, which is what I ask the judge to recommend.

Conceded in the sense that I agree on the framing, but it cuts against the rider, not for them: this is a rider-side cancellation (F4), so NS-0 sends it to NS-4, and the driver-side no-show branch the rider tries to borrow (NS-1/NS-2) is not the source of the fee at all.

This is the rider's own concession that the fee is prima facie valid; the cancellation at 08:46:40 against acceptance at 08:40:00 (F4) is 6 min 40 s, past the 3-minute line, so NS-4 gives no basis to refund and the recorded $6.61 (F7) stands unchanged.

Agreed the rider did not fail to show in the driver-cancellation sense — but the rider must not be allowed to convert a NS-4 fee into a review of the driver's arrival: GPS shows the driver was inside 200 m from 08:41:35 for a cumulative 5 min 5 s (F2, F5), so no part of the charge rests on delay or absence.

'Plans changed' (F10) is a change of mind, not a Ryde-recognised excuse; nothing in NS-4 makes fee liability depend on the rider's honesty, and I have never alleged rider misconduct, so no SAFE-1 screening arises either way in this file.

Proportionality is not a test in NS-4 — it is a fixed $6.61 fee, and the rider's own figures show my client waited a genuine 4 min 40 s stationary 41 m from the pickup after tapping "I'm Here" at 08:42:15 and staying inside 200 m for 4 min 25 s (F3, F6), so the wait was real, not nominal.

Profile facts cannot decide this case and I do not rely on them; for the record F17 is the rider's own brief, and the driver's history shows no route deviations and 699 trips in 90 days (F17), which is a high-volume driver, not an abusive cancellation pattern.
